title: Round-trip floating values and raw BFloat16 payloads
goal: Persist finite floating-point values in readable hexadecimal form, or use explicit-endian raw bits when signed zeros and NaN payloads must survive unchanged.

selectionNotes: Hex floating text preserves tested finite bits and signed zero; NaN text does not promise its payload.
Raw BFloat16 wire bytes use explicit big-endian order; native BitConverter byte order is not a portable protocol.

prerequisites: SDK console project targeting net11.0 with ImplicitUsings=enable and Nullable=enable. Import System.Buffers.Binary, System.Globalization and System.Numerics; place the supplied partial class in namespace Playbook.Samples.
constraints: Hex floating text preserves tested finite bits and signed zero; NaN text does not promise its payload.
Raw BFloat16 wire bytes use explicit big-endian order; native BitConverter byte order is not a portable protocol.
Framework-provided managed APIs; no additional NuGet package/assets, workload, provider or rendering mode. No older-target package route, AOT or native-device execution is established.
stabilityLimitations: Verified using .NET 11 RC2; GA reconciliation remains pending. These selected contracts have no publisher experimental annotation or required opt-in.

evidence.scope: Real older/newer runs compare double bit patterns for 19.375, negative zero, smallest subnormal, maximum finite and a negative fraction. Newer execution also checks float/Half hex, raw BFloat16 payloads, byte order, native BitConverter pairing, short buffers and observed NaN normalization. Actual managed execution; no mocks, cross-compilation or GA verification.
